findings.reason: implemented literally the node either adds an inert file that proves nothing about the skip rule or, if it adds a real record and the case goes red, treats a correct fresh answer as a failure; the case must be scoped to reads of the covered docs tree (read_plan/roadmap/audit's document set) with a non-review file, and the review-store reads stated as deliberately out of the covered set.
findings.text: §2's second done-when case asserts "A file added under the reviews tree changes no read's answer", but `docs/state/<project>/reviews/` is exactly the committed review store (`committed_review_root`, reckon/crew/review.py:2397-2416), which `list_plan_reviews` globs directly (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:1446-1457) and `review_coverage` consumes from `edit_plan` (reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:2177, whose returned `uncovered` set is the answer) and from admission's launch gate (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:3305) — so a valid added review record changes those very answers

findings.reason: as written the node ships a green "at most once" count with two BeautifulSoup parses reduced to one at best, two HTMLParser parses untouched and the prose-based digest/coverage answer still costing a full parse per snapshot, so §6's stated mechanism does not deliver the read cost the section is named for.
findings.text: §6's fourth change says `plan_review.review_coverage` reads stored snapshots "through the same persisted parse as §3", but `_snapshot_evidence` takes four parses per snapshot and the change reaches one: `_section_digests(text)` calls `_digest_state` → `_as_state(text)` → `_plan_html.read_state(text)` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:429-442, 315-331), `_snapshot_declarations(text)` calls `_plan_html.read_state(text)` again (:896-905), and `_prose_texts(text)` feeds `_structural_spans` — a second, independent HTML parser — twice (:445-478, reckon/_plan_html.py:394-398); §3's persisted entry is keyed on a file path and its stored value is the `read_state` mapping, so it cannot serve the prose reader at all, and the sixth done-when's counter (`_plan_html.read_state`) cannot see the two `_structural_spans` parses

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `metadata_index.discovery_file_scope` (reckon/metadata_index.py:100), `metadata_index._walk_covered` (:1157) and `_reuse_covered` (:870), `reckon/mcp.py` line 2224 (the `discovery_file_scope` entry in `_roadmap_tool`), `_plan_html.read_state_and_text_file` (reckon/_plan_html.py:1560), `plan_review.review_coverage` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:966), `queue_landing`'s `land_once` (reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:783), `queue_admission.advance_waiting_requests` (:2923) and its `_readiness_rows` (:2034), `_store._declared_north_stars` (reckon/_store.py:782), `project_state.project_state_mode` (reckon/project_state.py:317) and `resources._directory_identity_index` (reckon/resources.py:823) all resolve; the extensionless plan hrefs resolve as `<path>.html`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's second done-when case, "A file added under the reviews tree changes no read's answer", is false as stated: `docs/state/<project>/reviews/` is the committed review store, and `edit_plan` and admission answer from it.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §7 writes its log to its own fragment directory under `docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-costs-what-changed/` (the convention in `skills/reckon-build/references/sprint-orchestration.md`:422) and under the run's `logs/`; both survive the run.
rubric_items.naming: pass — s2, s6 and s7 name mechanisms (`discovery_file_scope`, `land_once`, `read_state_and_text_file`) and carry no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §6's fourth change names "the same persisted parse as §3" for review snapshots, but §3's persisted entry is keyed by a file path and cannot serve the three other parses each snapshot takes per call.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each section names one deliverable; §2's two changes and §6's four changes all serve one goal (one validation per request; every hot path reading through the memo), and §6's fourth change (review snapshots through the persisted parse) is that same goal rather than a second one.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — every entry in `plan-section-depends-on` resolves: s7 → s2–s6, s4 → s2, s3 → s2, s6 → s2, s3 and `work-is-never-stuck-behind-the-admission-loop#s19` (that plan exists and carries a `data-id="s19"` section); `informs`/`blocks` both name an existing plan; §7's two-arm base/head measure is declared after the sections it compares.
